text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Central bank DNB president Wim Duisenberg says that EMU stability pact will increase (budgetary) flexibility. (p1)
- Economic affairs and justice ministries launch restoration operation to prevent disquiet following the so-called Securitel judgement. (p1)
- Dutch software companies have too little innovation capacity to survive the dynamism in their market. (p3)
- Cleaning companies see their combined 1996 turnover rise 1.5 pct to Dfl 3.9 bn from Dfl 3.8 bn in 1995. (p49)
- Employers association VNO-NCW wants share option schemes for management and staff to be included in companies' annual reports. (p5)
VOLKSKRANT
- ING bank plans to auction unique library of former Ster disposable cutlery plant owner Joost Ritman. (p1)
- Labour party PvdA ideologist annoyed by rigidity of fellow party member and PM Wim Kok. (p4)
- Green party says environmentalists ought to play a role in Dutch collective bargaining economy. (p4)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Parliament wants rapid clarification of cabinet's long silence about invalid laws. (p2)
- Organisation of employers and employees divided on part- time labour. (p1)
- Creditors of now bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker can report their claims until October, 1. (p11)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- PTT Telecom and Libertel join forces against plans of traffic minister Annemaire Jorritsma for a retrospective collection. (p9)
TROUW
- Green party leader Paul Rosenmoeller thinks cabinet should ban short-distance flights from Schiphol airport to London, Paris and Frankfurt. (1)
- Supermarkets predict the end of the food specialty shops, according to poll. (p6)
